title: 2011 AMC 8 Problem 12
statement: Angie, Bridget, Carlos, and Diego are seated at random around a square table, one person to a side. What is the probability that Angie and Carlos are seated opposite each other?

solutions.text:
Consider that Angie’s seat is chosen. Carlos has an equal probability of being in any of the other \(3\) seats. Only one of them is opposite Angie, however. Therefore, the probability is \(\dfrac{1}{3}.\)

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Carlos has three possible seats, only one opposite Angie.
Fix Angie in one seat by symmetry.
